A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-PV study. Their text, tables, figures, equations, experimental Appendix A, and proof Appendices B–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original algorithmic and tabular classification experiments, length-generalization tests, data-scaling experiments, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds model/tool comparisons, prompt-sensitivity results, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains fixed-prompt proposal sampling, compilation/filtering, and selection by held-out validation error, without gradient updates or validation-driven proposal adaptation. Additional backbone and tool-use configurations are evaluated, but no redesign of the proposed algorithm is established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 synthetic tasks and five tabular datasets, including the retained length-generalization and data-scaling scenarios. The added experiments vary models, tools, and prompts within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5-Thinking ICL with and without tools, Gemini-3.1-Pro ICL with tools, and GPT-5-Thinking implementations of MLAgentBench and AIDE-ML with tools. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set beyond v2's retained baselines.

E3.justification: v3 introduces additional proposer configurations, explicit tool/no-tool controls, and a five-prompt evaluation at n=100. Its new runtime protocol reports seconds per sample and times SGD/FT using the minimum epochs needed for perfect training accuracy. These supplement the retained accuracy protocols and data splits.

E4.justification: New analyses test dependence on proposer capability and tool access, sensitivity to prompt wording, and training-versus-inference cost. Table 1 and Appendix A.3.3–A.3.4 substantially extend the retained SGD hyperparameter sweeps, length tests, and reasoning traces.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly summarizes variation across five prompt templates, including 82.5±3.1 for IsPrime+47. This reports prompt-dependent variability, not a documented increase in repeated runs or seeds. The existing tabular uncertainty entries remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, including v2's LLM-PV row, now identified as GPT-5-Thinking with tools. New results expose substantial configuration dependence, such as 50.4% on 10-P without tools versus 100% with tools. Tables 7–8 add prompt accuracies and runtime measurements; these are new results, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The finite-class generalization bound, proposal-mass validation guarantee, quantization analysis, and SGD lower-bound arguments remain unchanged, including their appendix proofs. Proposition and theorem numbering changes do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims about computationally accessible program search, sample-efficient rule recovery, length generalization, and auditability. The added evidence and expanded discussion elaborate and qualify these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 5.3 and 6 add substantive explanations distinguishing program search from direct label prediction and generic ML agents. They emphasize dependence on capable proposers and active testing, discuss training/inference cost tradeoffs, and identify longer, more compositional, or prior-misaligned programs as potential failure conditions.

D1.justification: v3 adds five explicit prompt templates, model/tool configuration information, and runtime measurement details. However, it removes v2's code-availability sentence and repository hyperlink. Detailed settings for the newly added agents remain incompletely documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al. (2024) for MLAgentBench and Jiang et al. (2025) for AIDE, positioning LLM-PV against general-purpose ML agents. The broader related-work discussion is retained. Splitting Solomonoff's combined reference into Parts I and II does not add previously uncited work.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed, the closing discussion is expanded into a numbered Section 6, and an Impact Statement and additional analysis subsections are inserted. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one column to two, substantially relocating and resizing figures and tables. Table 1 gains grouped model/tool rows, and new Tables 6–8 display prompts, sensitivity results, and runtimes. The original hyperparameter table becomes Table 9; existing plot content is retained.

improvement.justification: Table 1 substantially addresses v2's lack of comparisons separating backbone capability, tool access, and program search through GPT-5 controls and agentic baselines. Prompt sensitivity, measured costs, and explicit scope limitations make the central findings substantially better supported and qualified. The removed code link and incomplete new-agent settings weaken reproducibility, but do not outweigh these important evidential gains.
